justifications.functional_suitability: Patient Intake Container, Scheduling Engine Container (Resource Allocation Coordinator locking, Conflict Resolution Service), EMR Workspace Container with Audit & Event Emitter, and Billing & Claims Container cover R-01 to R-04. Gaps: no patient-facing portal and EMR internals lack a persistence component.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Distributed L2 Cache (Redis), Go/gRPC EMR Workspace, Citus sharding, PgBouncer, analytical read replicas, and Redpanda async events support the <1 s P95 target. Gaps: no explicit load targets or autoscaling, and the cache holds only session state.
justifications.compatibility: Integration & FHIR Mediator (HAPI FHIR R4, SMART-on-FHIR, mTLS) and FHIR APIs to External Lab & Imaging Systems address R-08. Gaps: EMR Workspace connects directly to labs, bypassing the mediator, with no mediator container-level relationships; claims use generic REST/SOAP.
justifications.usability: All six user groups reach the system via Envoy / NGINX API Gateway over HTTPS, but no UI containers (web app, patient portal) exist. Grafana UI serves compliance reporting, yet there are no role-specific interfaces.
justifications.reliability: Citus Worker Nodes with synchronous replication, Redpanda Raft consensus, Outbox Processor, DLQ, and Redis active-active geo-replication help. Gaps: no explicit active-active deployment for services, no failover or backup/DR design, and a single Coordinator Node.
justifications.security: MFA, TLS 1.3, mTLS, and OIDC in the Authentication Filter; WAF; PHI Crypto Middleware with Tink and KMS; Vault; Falco; immutable audit logs; Tiered Storage Encryption Interceptor; GDPR Purge & Tombstone Controller. Strong match to R-05 and HIPAA/GDPR.
justifications.maintainability: Clear service decomposition with layered components (router, service, repository), event-driven decoupling via Event Broker, and an Observability Stack. Weaknesses: polyglot stack raises overhead, some component diagrams are incomplete, and the Patient Intake component view wrongly embeds external containers.
justifications.portability: Kubernetes-oriented, vendor-neutral technologies (Redpanda, PostgreSQL/Citus, Envoy, Vault) with S3-compatible tiered storage and KMS or on-prem HSM suit the hybrid on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1 targets. Gaps: no explicit deployment view, with Cloud KMS and Redis Enterprise as dependencies.

sensitivity_points: Per-read column decryption and KMS key fetch latency
Cache hit ratio for hot session state
tradeoffs: Application-level encryption costs latency versus security
PERF-01.justification: Go/gRPC, Redis cache and PgBouncer pooling support sub-second loads, but no cache of clinical data, no latency budget, and crypto overhead are unaddressed. The cache holds only session state. Plausible, unproven.

sensitivity_points: Ingestion throughput of Camel transformation and DB writes
Resource isolation between ingestion and EMR reads
tradeoffs: Async buffering gives throughput but delays visibility
Schema validation costs throughput versus integrity
PERF-02.justification: Redpanda buffering and Camel K scaling suit the burst, but the path from mediator to EMR persistence is undefined (no relationship to the DB or EMR). Read isolation exists only through analytical replicas. Needs significant design.

elements: Identity Provider (IdP) with local on-premise cache proxy
sensitivity_points: Cross-site replication mode and failover detection time
Global traffic routing mechanism between sites
tradeoffs: Synchronous cross-site replication gives zero data loss but adds latency
AVAIL-01.justification: Hybrid regions are stated, and Raft, synchronous replicas and Redis geo-replication help. But there is no deployment view, no global load balancing or failover design, and cross-site DB replication is unspecified. One-minute RTO with no data loss is unsupported.

sensitivity_points: Failover time of the Citus coordinator
Idempotency of claim submission to external processors
tradeoffs: Synchronous replication protects data but raises write latency
Outbox gives reliability but at-least-once duplicates
AVAIL-02.justification: Synchronous shard replicas and the transactional outbox protect against loss, but the coordinator has no stated HA. There is no idempotency key or retry design for external submission, so duplicates are a risk, and the 30 s recovery is unproven.

sensitivity_points: Adapter interface stability toward Claims & Invoicing Engine
Shared billing data model across clearinghouses
tradeoffs: Single adapter is simple but may need a plugin abstraction
Isolation from EMR versus duplicated integration logic
MOD-01.justification: A dedicated Payment & Clearinghouse Adapter inside Billing isolates external integration, and EMR is a separate container, so change is confined. However, no explicit per-provider strategy or abstraction is defined, so a new clearinghouse may touch the adapter internals.

sensitivity_points: Schema migration process for Citus-sharded tables
Absence of any UI container in the model
tradeoffs: Layered Intake components keep change local but couple schema to repository
Event schema registry adds validation versus extra change
MOD-02.justification: Intake components are layered and audit events are published, so about three components may change (router, service, repository) plus the DB schema. But no UI container exists, and schema migration and audit trail propagation are undefined.

elements: Identity Provider (IdP) with local on-premise cache proxy
sensitivity_points: IdP enforcing MFA and token claims verification
Alert path from failed logins to security alert
tradeoffs: IdP token caching boosts availability but delays revocation
Centralised gateway auth is simple but a single choke point
SEC-01.justification: TLS with MFA is stated and the gateway validates tokens against the IdP, so a password alone should fail. But the model does not show failed-login alerting within 1 minute; Falco covers kernel events only and the SIEM is not modelled.

sensitivity_points: Absence of policy-enforcement component for treating relationships
tradeoffs: Immutable audit retention conflicts with GDPR erasure
Audit emission on every read adds latency
SEC-02.justification: Audit emitter, immutable logs and tiered storage with 10-year retention exist, but no access policy check (relationship-based authorization) is modelled, no tamper-evidence is described, and the emitter has no wiring. Purge controller may undermine audit integrity.
